## Natural history notes

A medium-sized longhorn beetle characterized by its elongated body, long antennae, and bold black-and-yellow banded pattern that gives it a zebra-like appearance. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, gardens, and other wooded or flower-rich habitats where adult beetles visit blooms for nectar and pollen. The larvae develop in dead or decaying wood, helping break down woody material, while adults are often seen on flowers or vegetation during warm months.
